raw_response:
I’m still going with wheat-maize on all 3.8 mu. That’s what I know best, and on such a small piece of land I can’t afford to take big risks. I’ve farmed this way many years. Wheat gives me steady grain, and maize follows right after, so even if one season is only average, the whole year can still work out. I finished the last cycle knowing fertilizer and water cost more than before, so this year I won’t push too hard, but I also won’t cut too much. If I save too much on fertilizer and the crop comes out weak, that loss is bigger than the little money saved. For wheat, I’ll sow in early October like usual, use a local improved variety people around here trust, put most fertilizer as base, then topdress once at jointing if the stand looks decent. Wheat needs water at the key times, so I’ll probably irrigate about 3 times if rainfall is normal. After wheat harvest in June, I’ll move quickly into maize because the window is short. I won’t do fancy tillage, just a simple quick field prep and sow. For maize, I’ll use hybrid seed, put fertilizer mainly at planting and a little more later, and irrigate only if the rain doesn’t come right. My wife and I can handle most of the labor ourselves on 3.8 mu, maybe with a little hired machine help if timing gets tight.
